new_scholarship.name: Perimeter Institute PhD Residency Program Award
new_scholarship.funding_type: Doctoral funding package (university salary plus Perimeter top-up)
new_scholarship.description: Perimeter Institute awards a PhD Residency Program Award to doctoral students admitted to a partner Canadian university and supervised by a Perimeter faculty member, associate faculty member or senior researcher. The official page states that resident PhD students are financially supported through their home university, typically for four years or twelve academic terms, and that the Residency Award adds top-up funding up to $30,000 per year, calculated after fees and tuition, on a September to August academic year, until Term 12. Benefits also include a dedicated desk in a shared workspace, access to Perimeter facilities, a 50% discount at the on-site Black Hole Bistro, and a technology grant of up to $2,000.

new_scholarship.application_period: Expression of Interest submitted November to January, within one week of the partner-university application; partner universities issue offers February to March; Perimeter contacts selected students April to May; arrival in Waterloo August to September.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Applicants must apply to a PhD programme at one of Perimeter's listed partner universities (Dalhousie, McMaster, University of Guelph, University of Toronto, University of Waterloo, Western, York) with a Perimeter-affiliated supervisor, and must submit a separate Expression of Interest to the Residency Award.

new_scholarship.description: The Janelia Research Campus of the Howard Hughes Medical Institute runs two fully-funded graduate training programmes with Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, in neuroscience and in cross-disciplinary biology (XDBio). Students apply directly to the Johns Hopkins Neuroscience programme in the autumn, naming one to four Janelia group leaders in the Statement of Interest; the published deadline for completed applications including letters of recommendation is December 3, and decisions are communicated by April 15. Janelia states that graduate scholars are fully supported financially by their labs and the graduate programme during their research, with a first-year Johns Hopkins stipend plus health insurance while in Baltimore, and a Janelia Graduate Scholar stipend, health insurance and travel support while at Janelia.

new_scholarship.description: Mexico's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, through AMEXCID, invites foreign nationals to study in Mexico under the Becas de Excelencia del Gobierno de México para Extranjeros. The 2026 call was offered to more than 170 countries and covered 90 Mexican higher education institutions whose programmes are registered in the National Postgraduate System. Benefits stated in the official call include a monthly stipend of four times the UMA for undergraduate and master's mobility and of five times the UMA for doctoral and postdoctoral research fellowships, enrolment and tuition fees, health insurance through the Mexican Social Security Institute, exemption from Mexican visa fees, international airfare in economy class on successful completion, and domestic transportation to the host city.
